Forty comments

Identity theft?

Curiously enough, Frankie Gavin’s Frankie Goes to Town has a track he calls, “The Maid Behind the Barrel” . It is in Em, of course tuned up to Fm as is Frankie’s preference.
The liner notes even say it it sometimes called “Kiss The Maid Behind the Barrel”.
It is quite different from this tune, a great new version of which is on Danu’s “All Things Considered”
Anybody else rune into this?

↳ Posted by RexMcGee on May 11th, 2002.

Pipe standard tune

I learnt this tune in a pipe lesson (intermediate level) at the Willy weel in Milltown Malbay.
The tune was used to show us to have lot of g roll practice…
It was about this version and under this name. I think it is a Seamus Ennis tune.

Also check out The Mountain Road, a collection of South Sligo musicians. This tune is the first tune on that album.

Kissing maids behind stuff

Here’s the ABCs for a piper’s version that would have all the rolls urs is talking about. It might be Paddy Keenan’s version, it’s from a tape someone gave me of stuff that was on the radio years ago and it sounds like him playing. Also, it can’t be Seamus Ennis‘ tune, as urs suggests, because it shows up in O’Neill’s -- which was published at the turn of the 20th Century. Seamus Ennis was born in 1919.

Kiss the Maid Behind the Barrel - Peadar O’Loughlin’s setting

I heard Maeve Donnelly And Peadar O’Loughlin on Clare fm discussing their “older” settings for tunes on their recording, “The Thing Itself.” Here’s the abcs for Kiss the Maid Behind the Barrel based on that recording. I find it very enjoyable to play on flute.

X:1
T:Kiss The Maid Behind The Barrel
S:Maeve Donnelly And Peadar O’Loughlin: The Thing Itself
Z:Jack Gilder
M:4/4
L:1/8
R:reel
K:Gmaj

↳ Posted by slainte on April 1st, 2006.

By the way, I’ve been playing the Steampacket as an easy substitute, but I really have to learn this in a couple of weeks. (Actually the first two parts are not exactly the same as the Steampacket.) I heard it played 2 or 3 times while I was travelling around in GB & NI quite recently. Definitely one of classic flute tunes often associated with John McKenna. Cathal McConnell recorded on his first album, Paul McGrattan did with Paul O‘Shaughnessy, and Peadar O’Loughlin recently did with Maeve Donnelly. Thanks Jack for their transcription.

Splitting The Already- Split Hair…(Sliabh Luachra Version 2.0)

Got this setting from Kerry box player Paudie O‘Connor’s collaboration with piper John O’Brien (Mick’s younger brother) entitled “Wind & Reeds”. Paudie says in the notes that he got this from fiddler Denis Murphy, hence the prefix I attached to the title:

X:1
T:Denis Murphy’s Kiss the Maid Behind the Barrel
S:Paudie O‘Connor & John O’Brien- “Wind & Reeds”
M:4/4
L:1/8
R:reel
K:Gmaj
DG ~G2 AG ~G2 | DG ~G2 cAGF | DG ~G2 AG (A/B/c) | defd cAGF |
DG ~G2 AG ~G2 | DG ~G2 cAFD | B4 c2 (A/B/c) | defd cAFA ||
dgfg agfg | dgfg agfe | df ~f2 affe | defd cAFA |
dg ~g2 bgfg | abag ({e}f3) g | afge fgeg | d2 eg fdcA ||:
~G2 dG EGdG | ~G2 dG cAFD | ~G2 dG DG (A/B/c) | defd cAFA :|
g2 bg agab | gabg defa | g2 bg agbg | defd cAFA |
g2 bg agab | gabg defg | abag ({e}f3) e | d2 ed cAFA ||
(B/c/d) BG (A/B/c) AF | (G2 ~G2) cAFA | BdBG A2 (A/B/c) | defd cAFA |
BdBG AF ~F2 | GBdB cAFA | (B2 ~B2) cA ~A2 | defd cAFA ||
GdAG G3 D | G2 Bd cAFA | GdAG G2 (A/B/c) | defd cAFA |
GdAG GD .D/.D/.D | GABd cAFD | (E/F/G) AB c2 (A/B/c) | defd cAGF ||

I thought it was different enough from enirehtac’s posting to include it here. Also, a helpful (hopefully) hint for our friend enirehtac (and anybody else posting ABC’s here): PLEASE write the ABC’s out four (4) measures per line. It prints out much nicer that way (& it’s a lot easier to read!). Thanks!

-Jay

The quartet (I think they were only four) sat in a semi-circle in a room to the left of the entrance, more or less facing us as we entered. Harry at the very right, then Colm, then Zoe, then the guitarist. At some point Colm started Conor Tully’s ( https://thesession.org/tunes/5337 ) and Harry played President Garfield ( https://thesession.org/tunes/419 ) in D - otherwise a fiddle friendly key, but not for this tune.

We stayed and listened for maybe half an hour, then found a session we could join (probably Queally’s or one of the two Cleary’s).

I don’t think I would have recognized Anthony Quigney. Maybe he was there, maybe he wasn’t, maybe they were different sessions.

↳ Posted by slainte on March 28th, 2021.

Kiss the Maid Behind the Barrel [6-part] (S: Denis Murphy, 1966)

Now that is a worthy opponent! It may be a leviathan of a transcription – but despite its ferocious looks, the 6-part version of Kiss the Maid Behind the Barrel is actually quite easy and fun to play. Denis Murphy makes the extra bits flow into one another so naturally, I’m now convinced that it is the standard version that lacks parts!

This time I transcribed both recordings of Denis playing the reel that I know of, in which he clearly chooses to play different variations for some of the parts. This is a reflection on how fruitless an “exact” transcription of a traditional musician may be if both variativity and the evolution of the tune within their own lifetime is not considered. Still, if used with an actual recording, I find that to be educational as a way of looking closely at what he did there – fiery stuff!

The first transcription comes from a tape which I believe is a partial copy of Breandán Breathnach’s Collection. After looking through the ITMA catalogue, I pinned down this particular recording session to 1966.

↳ Posted by Bregolas on April 5th, 2024.

Kiss the Maid Behind the Barrel [6-part] (S: Denis Murphy, Handed Down Archive)

The second transcription of Denis Murphy playing this reel comes from an undated donation to the Handed Down Sliabh Luachra Audio Archive published in 2020, which had already been linked above. You can listen to it here.

Headphones warning for the start of the track!

https://soundcloud.com/pj-teahan-884614828/denis-murphy-various-audio-donations-1

Note how in both cases Denis opts to end the tune with a variation on the finishing part that to me sounds like him imitating the pipes – expressly droning on A instead of the missing A roll on the fiddle :-)

GdAG G2 DG|~G2 Bd cAFA|GAAA G2 A/B/c|defd cAFD|
GAAA GAAA|GABd cAFD|E/F/G AB c2 A/B/c|defd cAFD|[G8B8]||

Re: Kiss The Maid Behind The Barrel [6-part] (Update)

Several more recordings of Denis playing the 6-part version of this reel have since come up – looks like it was one of his favourite party pieces! :-D

Just to update my previous post (https://thesession.org/tunes/676#comment988531), the source for this particular setting appears to have come from an undated reel-to-reel tape made by Séamus Ennis that was discovered in the attic of Denis Murphy’s home in Lisheen. This is an amazing recording overall that includes Ennis-Murphy duets that had never been published before!

https://soundcloud.com/pj-teahan-884614828/11a?in=pj-teahan-884614828/sets/seamus-ennis-visit-to-denis
